results.name: Financial Services Sector Cyber Threat Intel - Key Insights (February 2022)
results.description:
In February, an APT10 espionage group, believed to be from China, was linked to attacks on a local financial sector. The attacks started at the end of November 2021 and continued till February. The intrusions were tracked under the codename of Operation Cache Panda.

Other Major Incidents
Users of Monzo were targeted by phishing messages supported by a growing network of malicious websites. The BlackByte ransomware group targeted three organizations (including a financial entity) based in the U.S. An Antlion APT group was found to be using the 'xPack' backdoor against financial organizations. Medusa malware distributed through SMiShing service, named Cabassous and known for targeting the financial organizations in Turkey. LendUS discovered and then fixed a security incident.

results.name: China-Backed APT10 Targeted Taiwanese Financial Firms
results.description:
According to the security firm CyCraft, China's state-sponsored APT10 conducted a two-month campaign against Taiwanese financial services firms. CyCraft's analysis of the incident alleges that the attack used supply chain attacks to target software used by Taiwanese financial institutions.

The attackers first breached the software systems using a web service vulnerability present in security software, then deployed QuasarRAT and used it to download other malware payloads. CyCraft suggests that attackers were trying to steal financial information as the RAT is an open-source tool that can capture screenshots, edit registry, record webcam, steal passwords, and perform keylogging.

results.name: Chinese Hackers Target Taiwan's Financial Trading Sector with Supply Chain Attack
results.description:
An advanced persistent threat (APT) group operating with objectives aligned with the Chinese government has been linked to an organized supply chain attack on Taiwan's financial sector. The attacks are said to have first commenced at the end of November 2021, with the intrusions attributed to a threat actor tracked as APT10, also known as Stone Panda, the MenuPass group, and Bronze Riverside, and known to be active since at least 2009.

The second wave of attacks hit a peak between February 10 and 13, 2022, according to a new report published by Taiwanese cybersecurity firm CyCraft, which said the wide-ranging supply chain compromise specifically targeted the software systems of financial institutions, resulting in "abnormal cases of placing orders."

results.name: NICKEL targeting government organizations across Latin America and Europe
results.description: MSTIC has observed NICKEL, a China-based threat actor, targeting governments, diplomatic entities, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) across Central and South America, the Caribbean, Europe, and North America. MSTIC has been tracking NICKEL since 2016 and observed some common activity with other actors known in the security community as APT15, APT25, and KeChang.

results.name: Learning to ChaCha with APT41
results.description: Straight from the sunny UK to the stage of SAS-at-Home 2021, John Southworth (PwC) will be giving some insights about the threat actor APT41, also known as Red Kelpie and Winnti. Starting with APT10 (Red Apollo), the presentation will dance you through the malware used by APT41 – the Motnug loader and its descendant, the ChaCha loader, to some thoughts on the actor’s attribution and the payload, including the infamous CobaltStrike.

results.name: APT10: Sophisticated Multi-Layered Loader Ecipekac Discovered in A41APT Campaign
results.description: A41APT is a long-running campaign with activities detected from March 2019 to the end of December 2020. Most of the discovered malware families are fileless malware and they have not been seen before. One particular piece of malware from this campaign is called Ecipekac (a.k.a DESLoader, SigLoader, and HEAVYHAND). It is a very sophisticated multi-layer loader module used to deliver payloads such as SodaMaster (a.k.a DelfsCake, dfls, and DARKTOWN), P8RAT (a.k.a GreetCake, and HEAVYPOT) and FYAnti (a.k.a DILLJUICE stage2) which loads QuasarRAT.

results.name: APT10
results.description:
Origin: China, 2009

Aliases: Cloud Hopper, Red Apollo, CNVX, Stone Panda, MenuPass, POTASSIUM, MenuPass Group, APT 10

Key Target Sectors: Construction and Engineering, Aerospace, and Telecom firms, and Governments

Attack Vectors: Spear phishing, Spam Email, Data-theft, Typosquatting, Unauthorized Access, Phishing, Backdoor

Target Region: North America, South-East Asia, Eastern Asia, Western Europe 

Malware Used: Haymaker, Bugjuice, Snugride, QuasarRAT, RedLeaves, PlugX, PoisonIvy and ChChes

Tools Used: Certutil, Cmd, Impacket, Mimikatz, Net, Ping and PsExec

Vulnerabilities Exploited: Eternalromance Exploit (CVE-2017-0143)
